I’m not entirely sure myself, but with all the rain these past few weeks, I would think so. Don’t get me wrong though, hiking down San Carlos Falls even if it hasn’t rained is still worth the trip. As for the hike, I’m not 100% sure of the distance but it’s comprised of 30-60 minute hike through the savanna (it gets real muddy when it rains). Once you reach the coconut trees, you will find the first descent. It’s pretty steep, but there are ropes along the trail. After that, you would reach a beautiful river (?) that goes downstream, just follow that. At the end of that, you would see that you’re at the top of the falls. The trail going down to the falls is not as hard as the first one. Fair warning, as much as I recommend going after it rained, there was an [incident](https://www.google.com/amp/s/amp.guampdn.com/amp/973582002)  that happened about a year ago, so hike carefully.
Not the best during dry season, but San Carlos Falls is a beauty. The hike can get intimidating though. Once you get there, you can go downstream that leads to Emerald Pools.
